teams.heading: Maro Itoje feels rejuvenated after taking a break from England duty
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has reflected on his summer sabbatical, describing the experience as a vital period for mental and physical recovery. After an intense campaign, head coach Steve Borthwick suggested the forward take time away, leading him to miss England’s July fixtures. Itoje confirmed he feels refreshed ahead of the new season, stating, “I don't regret it at all.” Having returned to his first full pre-season with Saracens since 2014, he is now targeting a strong return to the international stage.

teams.heading: Jack Crowley ruled out until new year as Ireland face crisis
teams.body: Ireland’s fly-half options have been further restricted following confirmation that Jack Crowley remains sidelined until the new year. Currently recovering from a lower limb vascular injury sustained in April, the 26-year-old is officially ruled out of the upcoming November encounters against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan stated that "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority." With summer signing Will Harrison also nursing a knee injury, the selection picture for the position remains difficult.

lead.why: The sustained absence of a first-choice fly-half until the new year has immediate and significant implications for Ireland's upcoming November fixtures.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada banned under World Rugby’s match official abuse process
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has become the first individual sanctioned under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process. Following critical comments made regarding referee Luc Ramos after the loss to the All Blacks, the Argentine has been handed a two-Test suspension. This ruling prohibits him from all match-day proceedings, including stadium attendance, for the upcoming fixture against South Africa. While Quesada retains the right to appeal the decision, the governing body confirmed the ban remains in effect.

teams.heading: Former Wales international speaks out as concussion litigation increases in complexity
teams.body: The ongoing multi-million-pound concussion legal battle involving professional rugby remains active in the High Court. Recent coverage indicates that the litigation is growing in both scale and complexity, with a former Wales star releasing a statement as the proceedings continue. The case, which examines long-term brain injury in the sport, is still awaiting a final verdict. Supporters of the claimants maintain that the legal process is essential for addressing player welfare, while the broader implications for the professional game remain unresolved.

teams.heading: Les Kiss makes nine changes as Tom Wright hits 50th cap
teams.body: Coach Les Kiss has reshuffled his side for today's rematch in Mendoza, making nine alterations to the starting line-up. teams.heading: Japan Brave Blossoms Host Canada to Celebrate JRFU Centenary Match
teams.body: Japan host Canada at Denka Big Swan Stadium in Niigata City as part of the Lipovitan D Challenge Cup. The match marks the JRFU’s 100th anniversary, returning international rugby to the region for the first time in 18 years. Eddie Jones has made five changes to his side following their recent test against Australia, with Inoke Burua set to make his debut. Japan are ranked 12th globally, while Canada arrive in Niigata currently sitting 24th in the world rankings.

teams.heading: New Zealand fall to South Africa in tight Soweto series decider
teams.body: The All Blacks suffered a 29-24 defeat against South Africa at FNB Stadium on Saturday, conceding the three-match series 2-1. Despite a persistent attacking effort that saw Ardie Savea cross twice and a late consolation try from Samisoni Taukei’aho, New Zealand could not overcome a resilient Springbok side in the closing stages. The hosts pulled ahead through late scores from Jesse Kriel and Malcolm Marx, ensuring the visitors departed Johannesburg without the series honours in this latest instalment of the rivalry.

teams.heading: South Africa edge New Zealand 29-24 to take home-leg series lead
teams.body: South Africa secured a hard-fought 29-24 victory against New Zealand in Saturday's third Test at FNB Stadium to take a 2-1 series lead. The encounter lived up to its billing as a thriller, with both sides crossing for 4 tries. After a deadlocked 12-12 half-time score, the hosts surged ahead through second-half efforts from Jesse Kriel and Malcolm Marx. A late penalty from Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu proved decisive before New Zealand added a final consolation score after the clock turned red.
